title: Greenhouse effect diagram sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 14 (Greenhouse effect diagram sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 14: Global warming and the greenhouse effect. To understand how greenhouse gases warm the Earth and how human activity increases the effect

picture.alt: A diagram of the greenhouse effect
picture.draw: Draw and label: Greenhouse effect diagram sheet

questions.q: Describe the greenhouse effect in four steps.
questions.a: Sunlight warms the Earth; Earth gives off heat (infrared); greenhouse gases absorb some; they re-radiate it, keeping Earth warm.
questions.model: Step 1: sunlight reaches and warms the Earth. Step 2: the Earth gives off heat. Step 3: greenhouse gases absorb some of it. Step 4: they send some back down, so the Earth stays warmer.

questions.q: By how much did CO₂ rise from 1800 to 2024 (table)?
Is the ozone hole the same as global warming?
questions.a: No: the ozone layer protects from UV; global warming is extra trapped heat.

questions.q: Core: Write a paragraph explaining how burning fossil fuels contributes to global warming (portal response box). Start: 'When fossil fuels burn...'
questions.a: When fossil fuels burn they release carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas; more CO₂ absorbs and re-radiates more heat, so average temperatures rise.
questions.model: Teacher writes the model: Point: burning fossil fuels releases CO₂. Explain: CO₂ absorbs heat given off by Earth. Link: more CO₂ means more heat trapped, so global temperatures rise.

questions.q: Extend: Give two consequences of global warming.
questions.a: Rising sea levels, more extreme weather, melting ice, changes to habitats and crops.

questions.q: Stretch: 'CO₂ and temperature both rose, so one caused the other.' Is this good reasoning? Explain.
questions.a: Correlation alone does not prove cause; scientists also understand the mechanism and test it, which is why they are confident.

questions.q: Big question: if the greenhouse effect keeps us alive, why is it a problem?
questions.a: Extra greenhouse gases from human activity trap more heat, so the Earth warms beyond its natural balance.
